title: myColorado app offline after state finds cybersecurity incident; state estimates data of roughly 100,000 users involved
date_note: The state's page says the incident was found on the night of Nov. 18 (update dated Nov. 24); The Record and the Gazette also give Nov. 18.
org: Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT)
geo_basis: state agency as the sources state it; the state capital is used for the pin
summary: Colorado’s Governor’s Office of Information Technology says it is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving myColorado; KKTV reports OIT estimated data of between 50,000 to 150,000 individuals may be affected. KOAA reports OIT now says the data of roughly 100,000 users was involved, including PDFs and photographs of documents like passports, vehicle registrations and insurance cards; OIT said payment information was not involved.
plain: Colorado’s myColorado app is offline after a cybersecurity incident. KOAA reports the state says the data of roughly 100,000 users was involved, including photos of documents like passports; OIT said payment information was not involved.
exec: A state ID app is offline; OIT says, per KOAA, the data of roughly 100,000 users was involved, including passport, registration and insurance documents.
action: As the state's myColorado page advises, use your physical driver license or state-issued ID for identity verification and use agency websites for state services while the app is offline.

evidence.quote: OIT estimated that the cybersecurity incident may have impacted between 50,000 to 150,000 individuals' data.
The app has approximately 2.1 million users.
The data of roughly 100,000 myColorado users was involved in last week’s cybersecurity incident

validation.note: State of Colorado's own myColorado page (primary) and KKTV both state the incident and that the app is offline; the 50,000 to 150,000 estimate and Nov. 18 discovery are from KKTV (9News page returned 403; Krystal 93 repeats the estimate). The state's page also gives the 50,000 to 150,000 estimate and about 2.1 million app users. The Record and the Gazette (24 Nov) also report the incident, the Nov. 18 discovery, no restoration timeline and that affected users will be notified; the Gazette repeats the 50,000 to 150,000 estimate. The Record gives its own figure of nearly 150,000 and is not used for it.

review.note: date_note and validation note wrongly said state page gives no earlier day or figures; it gives Nov 18 and 50,000-150,000
